entries.clue: Supports - ticks (7)

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it, which is what a supporter at a meeting does
each tick of a clock marks off one unit of time, sixty of them to the minute

annotation.walkthrough: The dash is the whole disguise: two unrelated senses of one word sit either side of it, one from the committee room and one from the clock face.
annotation.definitionFit: Supports backs a motion the way a seconder does; ticks are the clock's own units — one word, two everyday senses.

entries.clue: Red insect with horn's noise entertaining King (8)

indicators.note: To entertain a guest is to have them in your house, so the word that entertains holds the other letter inside itself.

blocks.note: the three-letter insect a setter reaches for first
the noise a horn makes, written the way comics spell it
R is the crossword king, from the Latin Rex stamped on coins and documents

annotation.walkthrough: The insect and the horn belong to a garden afternoon, and 'entertaining King' sounds like a royal visit — nothing in the surface admits that a colour is being built.
annotation.definitionFit: Red: the deep purple-red of the vegetable is a colour in its own right, the shade a blushing face is said to go.

entries.clue: Lapel splotched with a saffrony mixture (6)

indicators.note: A splotched surface has had something flung at it and landed in blotches, so the letters arrive in no particular order.

blocks.note: five letters from the garment and one stray article, six in all, re-sorted into a Valencian rice dish

annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a stained jacket, which is exactly what a plate of this balanced on your knee would produce.
annotation.definitionFit: saffrony mixture: the dish is rice, seafood and vegetables cooked together in one pan and turned yellow by saffron, so it really is a tinted mixture.

entries.clue: A little prude can't eradicate provider of vino (8)

indicators.note: Asking for a little of a phrase is asking for a short piece of the letters themselves, not for a word that means something smaller.

blocks.note: eight letters run without a break from the end of the first word, through the whole of the second and into the third; the apostrophe is no obstacle

annotation.walkthrough: 'Can't eradicate' reads as a stubborn stain and the prude as the person complaining about it. The three words are only a letter run.
annotation.definitionFit: provider of vino: the glass jug wine is poured into and served out of at table, so it is what supplies your glass.

entries.clue: 'Lavish' starter for lunch covered in young insects sent back (4-2)

indicators.note: A starter is the first thing to arrive, so what is taken from the word after it is the letter it begins with.
To be covered in something is to have it all round you, so the letter ends up inside the other piece rather than beside it.
Something sent back retraces the way it came, so those letters are written out in the opposite order.

blocks.note: a pupa is an insect at its second stage, between grub and adult
the opening letter of the meal, and nothing else of it

annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' pulls double duty: on the surface it is the first course of the lavish meal, in the wordplay the first letter of the word after it.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Lavish': a slap-up meal is a generous, no-expense-spared spread — British informal, and lavish is precisely the sense meant.

entries.clue: Rotten luck, Ken: a horrible kind of 'sandwich' (7)

indicators.note: Something rotten has decayed out of its proper shape, so the letters it labels do not keep the order they are given in.

blocks.note: seven letters from the two words, the K turning up twice, redealt

annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one friend commiserating with another, and the quotation marks are the only hint that the sandwich is not lunch.
annotation.definitionFit: a horrible kind of 'sandwich': a knuckle sandwich is British slang for a punch in the mouth, so the answer is the word that heads that compound.

entries.clue: Almond cake consumed in Jarbidge, Nevada (6)

indicators.note: What has been consumed has been swallowed whole by what surrounds it, so the letters sit unbroken inside the words that follow.

blocks.note: six letters run straight on from the end of the town's name into the start of the state's, comma and all

annotation.walkthrough: Jarbidge is a real Nevada town, and it is in the clue for one reason: its last two letters and the state's first four sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Almond cake: a Geneva cake is the dense French bake made with ground almonds in place of flour, so a city's name doubles as a recipe.

entries.clue: Vino - cheese (not started) - then cocktail (8)

indicators.note: A word that is not started has lost the letter it begins with, so what is left runs from the second letter on.

blocks.note: brie is the cheese, and lopping off the letter it opens with leaves three
a sling is a long mixed drink — gin sling, Singapore sling

annotation.walkthrough: The dashes make the clue look like three items on a wine list. Only the middle one is a word to be trimmed.
annotation.definitionFit: Vino: a German white grape and the wine pressed from it, so the slangy word for wine defines the answer by kind.

entries.clue: Pungent ingredient presenting unfortunate gastric ordeal (7,6)

indicators.note: An unfortunate turn of events is one that has not gone as planned, and letters called unfortunate have likewise ended up somewhere other than where they belong.

blocks.note: thirteen letters across the two words, redealt to fill the seven and the six

annotation.walkthrough: Both halves of the clue describe the same dinner from opposite ends — what went into it, and what it did afterwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Pungent ingredient: roasting mellows garlic, but it still goes into a dish for the strong smell and taste that pungent names.

entries.clue: Everything I left over? An omelette and a cake (8)

indicators.note: Something turned over ends up facing the way it came from, so the assembled pieces are read out from their far end.

blocks.note: the everyday word for the whole of something
the pronoun is taken at face value, as the single letter it is written with
a Trot is a Trotskyist, British shorthand for someone well over on the political left

annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the turning instruction an across clue would use; it is a person instead, and the little word after it does the turning.
annotation.definitionFit: An omelette and a cake: a Spanish tortilla is a potato omelette, a Mexican one a flat maize cake — one word, both dishes.

entries.clue: A small image's showing jellies (6)

blocks.note: the clue's own first word, taken as the letter it is
S for small, as on a clothing label
a pic is a picture, the short form used in every newspaper office
the apostrophe-s reads as a possessive on the surface and hands over a letter in the wordplay

annotation.walkthrough: Everyman is fond of letting an apostrophe-s do a letter's work; here it is the S that makes the answer plural, which the enumeration never warns you about.
annotation.definitionFit: jellies: savoury meat or vegetable jellies set clear in a mould, so the plural noun swaps straight in.

entries.clue: Champion mostly having swallowed a liqueur (8)

indicators.note: A word taken mostly is written all but its final letter, since most of it is what is left once the end goes.
What swallows a thing takes it right inside, so the letter goes into the middle of the word rather than after it.

blocks.note: to champion a cause is to advocate it; docked of its last letter that leaves seven
the article is swallowed whole, as the single letter it is written with

annotation.walkthrough: Wordplay and drink share a root: advocaat is Dutch for a lawyer, and the thick egg-and-brandy drink was reckoned good for a pleader's throat.
annotation.definitionFit: liqueur: the thick, sweet Dutch egg-yolk-and-brandy drink is one of the sweetened spirits that word covers.

entries.clue: Before curt excuse, spill drink (6)

indicators.note: Putting one piece before another places it in front, so what the clue mentions second is written first.
A curt reply is cut short, and a word described that way gives up the letter at its end.

blocks.note: to tip a bucket over is to spill what is in it
a plea is an excuse, shortened here by a letter

annotation.walkthrough: The surface has someone apologising and knocking a glass over. Read as instructions it is the excuse that gets cut short, not the glass.
annotation.definitionFit: drink: your tipple is the drink you habitually take — 'what's your tipple?' — an everyday, slightly jocular noun.

entries.clue: Drunk at Conference perhaps suggesting compote (6,5)

indicators.note: The word admits an example rather than a synonym: one named variety is standing in for the whole class it belongs to.

blocks.note: stewed is long-standing slang for drunk
Conference is the commonest British pear variety, so a particular pear stands for the general kind

annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a delegate who has enjoyed the hospitality. The capital letter is the tell: Conference is a pear, not a venue.
annotation.definitionFit: compote: a compote is fruit simmered slowly in syrup, which is what the two words describe between them.

entries.clue: Catch intro to elegant music where one may drink elegantly (4,4)

indicators.note: An intro is the opening of a thing, so what is taken from the word after it is the letter it starts with.

blocks.note: to catch a prize is to win it
the first letter of the word, and no more of it
written music is divided into bars

annotation.walkthrough: The word 'elegant' works twice over: once to give up its opening letter, and once, as an adverb, to say what sort of drinking place is meant.
annotation.definitionFit: where one may drink elegantly: these sell wine by the glass in more genteel surroundings than a pub, so the phrase names them by function.

entries.clue: Dessert: the writer emits shrill laugh audibly (3,5)

indicators.note: What holds only audibly is judged by ear, so the letters follow the sound of the phrase and not its spelling.

blocks.note: a setter referring to himself in a clue is 'the writer', which on paper is one letter
to let out a shrill cry of laughter is to scream
said at speed the two words run together and a listener writes down something else entirely

annotation.walkthrough: The children's chant 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream' is built on exactly this: identical sounds, quite different spellings.
annotation.definitionFit: Dessert: the frozen sweet served at the end of a meal, so the general word covers the answer as one kind of pudding.

entries.clue: Every so often, Linus boils angrily - being this? (7)

definitions.note: The definition is a pointer rather than a synonym: 'this' is the state the clue has just painted — someone boiling with anger — and BILIOUS is the adjective for it.

indicators.note: Something done every so often is done at regular intervals, and the letters are taken at intervals too — every second one.
Doing a thing angrily is doing it wildly and with no care for order, so the letters land out of their proper places.

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of the name, picked out in turn
all five letters go into the mix, to be re-sorted along with the two above

annotation.walkthrough: 'Boils angrily' looks like the definition and is really fodder plus its instruction. The definition is the two words after the dash, pointing back at the whole picture.
annotation.definitionFit: being this?: the clue points at its own scene — bilious means liverish and bad-tempered, which is what a man boiling with anger is.

entries.clue: 'Unfinished, Cubistic' - confused, perhaps - snap! (7)

indicators.note: A word left unfinished stops short of its last letter, so the final C never reaches the mix.
Something confused has been jumbled into disorder, and letters in disorder are letters no longer in the sequence given.
The word flags an example rather than a synonym: one named kind is standing in for the whole family it belongs to.

blocks.note: the art word gives up its closing letter, and the seven that remain are redealt

annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and the dashes make the first two words look like a gallery label for a half-painted canvas. They are only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: snap!: a ginger snap or a brandy snap is a thin crisp biscuit, so the exclamation defines the answer by one of its kinds.

entries.clue: Home, once more begins to eat (4,2)

blocks.note: digs are lodgings — the British word for rented rooms you go home to
the words ask for home a second time, and someone who is in is at home

annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Home, once more' read as a weary arrival, when it is really an instruction to give a word for home twice over.
annotation.definitionFit: begins to eat: to dig in is to set about a meal with appetite — 'dig in!' is the invitation at the table — and the tense matches.

entries.clue: Plans sent back: Everyman's persistently irritating online (6)

indicators.note: Something sent back travels the way it came, so the letters of the word before it are written in the opposite order.

blocks.note: plans in the draughtsman's sense — street plans are maps
the setter signs himself Everyman, so his own possessive is these two letters

annotation.walkthrough: Everyman writes himself into his own wordplay: whenever this puzzle says 'Everyman's', it means 'my'. Worth remembering — he does it most weeks.
annotation.definitionFit: persistently irritating online: spammy describes the junk that keeps arriving unasked in an inbox, which is exactly that nuisance.

entries.clue: Yankiness yardstick? (5,3)

blocks.note: the invented noun asks what makes a thing American, which sends you hunting for a flag, a president or a state
a yardstick is what other things are measured against, and the phrase wanted is the one Americans use for something that could not be more American

annotation.walkthrough: 'As American as apple pie' is the set phrase, so the yardstick turns out to be a pudding. There is no wordplay here to find — the whole clue is one definition, told slant.
annotation.definitionFit: Yankiness yardstick?: the simile 'as American as apple pie' makes the pudding the standard measure of Americanness, which is a yardstick's job.

entries.clue: Gutted: canapés - mixed nuts (6)

indicators.note: A gutted fish has had its insides taken out, so the word loses the letter sitting at its dead centre.
Mixed things have been stirred about until nothing is where it started, which is what the remaining letters do.

blocks.note: the seven letters lose the one at the dead centre, and the six left over are re-sorted

annotation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is also British for bitterly disappointed, which is what the surface wants: the canapés have gone and only the bowl of nuts is left.
annotation.definitionFit: nuts: pecans are the sweet North American nuts of pie and praline fame, so the plural noun covers them as one kind.

entries.clue: Baking powder composed of bismuth, calcium and rubidium (6)

blocks.note: Bi is the chemical symbol for the element
Ca is the chemical symbol for the element
Rb is the chemical symbol for the element

annotation.walkthrough: 'Composed of' is doing double work: a compound is composed of elements, and so is this answer — three symbols off the periodic table, in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Baking powder: bicarb is bicarbonate of soda, the raising agent sold as baking soda and the working half of baking powder.

entries.clue: Sweet bits of lardons in coulis on arborio, perhaps (8)

indicators.note: A bit of a word is the smallest piece that still points at it — the letter it opens with — and each word in the run gives one up.

blocks.clueFragment: bits of lardons in coulis on
blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words after the instruction, taken in the order they come
arborio is the short-grain Italian variety used for risotto, so the named type stands for the grain itself

annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a menu of French and Italian oddments, and 'on' looks like joinery holding it together. It is the fourth word to give up a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweet: in Britain a sweet is a piece of confectionery, and this is the black aniseed-flavoured one sold in laces and pipes.

entries.clue: New recruit, Miles, gets curry powder (8)

indicators.note: A new arrangement is the old one broken up and set out differently, which is what these letters are put through.

blocks.note: all seven letters of the word go into the mix as they stand
M is the standard abbreviation for miles, as on a road sign

annotation.walkthrough: Miles is a man on the surface and a unit of distance in the wordplay; the two commas are what make him look like a person being introduced.
annotation.definitionFit: curry powder: turmeric is the yellow ground root that colours the blend, so the setter defines it by the mixture it goes into.

entries.clue: Necessity in alimentation; compound; indispensable nutrient, primarily! (6)

definitions.text: Necessity in alimentation; compound; indispensable nutrient, primarily!

indicators.note: Primarily means first of all, so what each word in the run hands over is the letter it starts with.

blocks.clueFragment: Necessity in alimentation; compound; indispensable nutrient
blocks.note: six words, six opening letters, read straight off in the order they are written

annotation.walkthrough: Every word is doing both jobs at once: read as a sentence the clue describes the vitamin, and read as an instruction each word gives up its initial.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: niacin is vitamin B3, an essential compound the body cannot make and has to take from food.
